record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.context_brief: indefinite Riccati equations in H-infinity control
record.original_question: Develop general existence and structural results for the indefinite algebraic Riccati equation A^T P + P A - P Sigma P + gamma^{-2} P V_1 P + R_{1,\infty} = 0 that arises in full-state-feedback H_infinity control. In this equation the quadratic term P (gamma^{-2} V_1 - Sigma) P may be indefinite, and the source notes that, aside from limited prior work, virtually no theory is available for such equations.

evidence.quote: In the full-state-feedback case, enforcement of the constraint ||G(s)||_infinity < gamma leads to ... (6.41).
Now the quadratic term P(gamma^{-2} V_1 - Sigma)P may be indefinite. With the exception of [64], virtually no results on the solutions to such indefinite Riccati equations are available.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, let $\Sigma, V_1, R_{1,\infty} \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be symmetric matrices, and let $\gamma > 0$ be a real parameter. Consider the indefinite continuous-time algebraic Riccati equation
$$A^{T} P + P A - P\,\Sigma\, P + \gamma^{-2} P\, V_1\, P + R_{1,\infty} = 0$$
for a symmetric matrix $P \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$. Equivalently, with $Q := \gamma^{-2} V_1 - \Sigma$, the quadratic term takes the form $P\,Q\,P$, where $Q$ is permitted to be indefinite (i.e., $Q$ need not be positive semidefinite or negative semidefinite).

Develop a general theory for such indefinite algebraic Riccati equations. Specifically:

(a) Give necessary and sufficient conditions on the data $(A, \Sigma, V_1, R_{1,\infty}, \gamma)$ for the existence of a real symmetric solution $P$, and for the existence of a stabilizing solution (one for which $A - \Sigma P + \gamma^{-2} V_1 P$ is Hurwitz).

(b) Describe the structure of the set of all real symmetric solutions, including ordering properties, extremal solutions, and the dependence of solutions on the parameter $\gamma$.

(c) Provide structural characterizations (e.g., via Hamiltonian or symplectic matrices, invariant Lagrangian subspaces, or matrix pencils) that account for the indefiniteness of $Q$.

The objective is a unified existence and structural theory comparable to that available for the classical (definite) algebraic Riccati equation.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on indefinite algebraic Riccati equations arising in H-infinity control since the problem was posed. Results include existence theorems for positive semidefinite and sign-indefinite stabilizing solutions via Hamiltonian/eigenvalue tests (Scherer; Wimmer), characterizations through invariant Lagrangian subspaces in indefinite inner product spaces (Ran-Rodman and others), and Popov-function factorization approaches. However, a fully general theory comparable to the definite case is not yet complete, and the problem is typically regarded as only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Existence Theorems for Positive Semidefinite and Sign Indefinite Stabilizing Solutions of H∞ Riccati Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of both positive semidefinite and sign indefinite stabilizing solutions of H∞-type Riccati equations is determined via joint eigenvalue and Hamiltonian tests.
status_evidence.claim: Existence conditions for stabilizing (possibly indefinite) solutions of H∞ Riccati equations have been established.

status_evidence.title: Stabilizing solutions of the H∞ algebraic Riccati equation
status_evidence.snippet: A stabilizing solution exists for all but finitely many γ larger than some bound; exception points are switching points where eigenvalues of the stabilizing solution can switch sign.
status_evidence.claim: Structural results on the γ-dependence of stabilizing solutions exist.

status_evidence.title: The Algebraic Riccati Equation and Its Role in Indefinite Inner Product Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Hermitian solutions can be studied via invariant Lagrangian subspaces of matrices self-adjoint in an indefinite inner product.
status_evidence.claim: Structural characterizations via indefinite inner product geometry are available.
